title.narrative: Sustainable Development Goals Indonesia One - Green Finance Facility (Phase 1)

description.narrative: The sovereign financial intermediary loan to Indonesia will be onlent to PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (PT SMI) for SIO-GFF implementation, to support achievement of the country's sustainable development goals (SDG's) through an innovative transition financing mechanism. The SIO-GFF mechanism will link funds provision to subprojects with clear green - a cross cutting theme across most SDGs - and financial bank-ability targets. Designed as a de-risking facility SIO-GFF aims to leverage ADB and government funds to catalyze a multiple of green funds from private, institutional and commercial sources over time. The project will play a critical role in Indonesia's sustainable economic recovery following the COVID-19 caused pandemic including through specific targeting of post-COVID-19 recovery projects. TA support will provide capacity and implementation support to PT SMI as well help propose future SIO phases and more innovative leveraged finance tools.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Green and SDG-impacting infrastructure projects (GSIPs) developed and approved for financing. Indicator: A pipeline of at least 20 GSIPs identified for potential SIO-GFF financing (OP 3.1; OP 6.1.2) Achievement: 5 Progress/Status: By November 2024: a pipeline of 20 green and SDG-impacting infrastructure projects (GSIPs) have been identified for potential SIO-GFF financing. This target is being achieved as of November 2024. PT SMI's continued efforts with the extended consultant support will facilitate the identification of additional qualified subprojects beyond the 2024. However, the success of identifying the additional qualified subprojects beyond 2024 is also subject to a favorable local and international economic and market condition. Data Source: SIO-GFF progress reporting included in PT SMI's annual reports

Output: Green and SDG-impacting infrastructure projects (GSIPs) developed and approved for financing. Indicator: At least 10 GSIPs with clear green or SDG indicators approved by PT SMI for SIO-GFF financing for a total project cost of at least $250 million, utilizing $150 million from ADB ordinary capital resources funds and the balance from non-SIO-GFF sources including PIC sources (OP 3.1; OP 6.1.2) Achievement: 5 Progress/Status: By November 2024, 6 qualified subprojects have been approved and 2 additional subprojects have been reviewed and pending for environmental clearances. In this connection, by 2026: the likelihood of success is very high for identifying at least 10 GSIPs with clear green or SDG indicators approved by PT SMI for SIO-GFF financing for a total project cost of at least $250 million, utilizing $150 million from ADB ordinary capital resources funds and the balance from non-SIO-GFF sources including PIC sources. This target is very likely to be achieved by 2026. Despite the challenging market condition, PT SMI is working closely with the consultants, subproject developers and other relevant stakeholders to develop qualified subprojects. The assessment is also based on PT SMI's strong commitment to develop a promising pipeline and any future corrective measures to be undertaken by ADB and PT SMI. Data Source: SIO-GFF progress reporting included in PT SMI's annual reports and TA completion report prepared by PT SMI

Output: Green and SDG-impacting infrastructure projects (GSIPs) developed and approved for financing. Indicator: At least 10 staff of PT SMI (at least 40% of whom are women), trained in (i) green frameworks and indicators, (ii) GSIP screening, selection, and monitoring approaches, (iii) innovative finance techniques, and (iv) developing SDG road maps and action plans (OP 6.1.2) Progress/Status: A number of gender related training has been completed. A capacity-building training on GESI Mainstreaming for Corporate and Project-Level Implementation was conducted on October 27, 2022, to support the implementation of PT SMI's GESI Mainstreaming Guidelines and Policy, which were officially adopted on October 1, 2020. A total of 15 participants attended the training, of whom 60% were women. A two-day training workshop was held in March 2024, covering the following topics: (i) green frameworks and indicators, (ii) GSIP screening selection and monitoring approaches, (iii) innovative finance techniques, and (iv) developing SDG roadmaps and action plans. The workshop was attended by 28 PT SMI staff members, including 15 women. Female participation rate is 54%. On October 31 and November 1 2024, the gender consultants held a workshop in Bogor to advance Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) in infrastructure projects. The training was attended by 32 participants, including 27 women (84%). The program included pre- and post-training assessments, which showed that 80% of participants demonstrated improved knowledge of GESI principles and their application in corporate and project contexts. Further training events are planned for late 2024 and in 2025. See the attached GAP monitoring sheet for details. This target is achieved. Data Source: PT SMI periodic (at least semiannual) progress reports Actual value:

Output: Green and SDG-impacting infrastructure projects (GSIPs) developed and approved for financing. Indicator: At least 50% of ADB financed GSIPs with integrated GESI approved (OP 6.1.2) Progress/Status: National and international GESI consultants were engaged to assist in preparing GESI mainstreaming strategies for all existing eight projects and upcoming SIO-GFF subprojects. All eight subprojects include Corrective Action Plan (CAP) requirements to implement GESI arrangements progressively, which have been incorporated into PT SMI's Environmental and Social Safeguard Standards. Technical Assistance (TA) consultants conducted gender screenings to identify potential GESI entry points within the subprojects. The subprojects gender screening document is available. Due to the relatively low number of subprojects, this target is unlikely be achieved. Change is needed. Data Source: PT SMI periodic (at least semiannual) progress reports Actual value:

Output: Green and SDG-impacting infrastructure projects (GSIPs) developed and approved for financing. Indicator: SIO-GFF operationalized (i) using the existing PT SMI lending systems for subproject origination, structuring, lending, and reporting, and (ii) applying SIO-GFF specific eligibility criteria for subproject selection and evaluation, including green-SDG-ESMS frameworks (OP 6.1.2) Progress/Status: By 2022: Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Indonesia One - Green Finance Facility (SIO-GFF) operationalized (i) using the existing PT SMI lending systems for subproject origination, structuring, lending, and reporting, and (ii) applying SIO-GFF specific eligibility criteria for subproject selection and evaluation, including green SDG-ESMS (environmental and social management system) frameworks. The SIO-GFF specific eligibility criteria have been applied since the first subproject approval in 2022, with processing improvements made for the following 5 subloan approvals in 2023. Two further new subprojects are being approval as of November 2024. This target is being achieved as of November 2024. The criteria in ADB project design and monitoring framework, project administration manual, and green and SDG indicators are being achieved. Detailed subproject reviews on financial, environmental, and social performances are also being achieved. Data Source: PT SMI periodic (at least semiannual) progress reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2022 Target value: Y
Private, institutional and commercial (PIC) investments catalyzed and blended with public sector funds to finance green and SDG-impacting subprojects, with a clear climate resilience impact created

At least $150 million in PIC financing catalyzed (approved commitments) (OP 3.1.1) Progress/Status: A total of $33,812,589 has been disbursed to PT SMI for a total of 6 approved subprojects. 1 for drinking water supply and 5 for mini-hydro power. Comparing to the target catalyzation level of 30% for green subprojects and 20% for SDG subprojects, the accumulative catalyzation rate of PIC finance for these 6 subprojects is about 59%. This translates to about $57 million equivalent based on the total existing subproject disbursement approval, about 33.5% against the implementation progress of 45.5% from June 2022 to November 2024. An additional $36,835,400 for 2 subprojects was disbursed to PT SMI in December 2024. Data Source: PT SMI periodic (at least semiannual) progress reports Actual value:

At least 15% of SIO-GFF funds approved for climate adaptive construction or rehabilitation infrastructure projects (OP 3.1.3) Progress/Status: 15% of the $150 million ADB finance is $22.5 million. TPT Dumai Tirta Persada; PLTM Karai 7; and PLTM Karai 13 are all climate adaptive construction or rehabilitation infrastructure projects with cumulative approvals of $28.6 million to November 2024 which is 127.1% of the 2027 target of $22.5 million (15% of $150 million). Data Source: SIO-GFF progress reporting included in PT SMI's annual reports Actual value:

Carbon dioxide emissions reduced by at least 120,000 tons per year (verified life cycle projections) (OP 3.1) Progress/Status: Estimated carbon dioxide emissions from the 5 renewable energy projects approved up to November 2024 amount to 104,000 tCO2 (once all 5 are in full production) which is 41.6% of the intended target (e.g., this target is to be achieved by 2027). Only 2 of the approved subprojects have reached the full operations stage (PT Karai 7; and PT Karai 13) and can be measured. Actual reductions in emissions from these 2 subprojects are exceeding targeted total levels of 85,900 tCO2 p.a. (based on annualizing data available for the first half of 2024). As a full year of operations data is not yet available the results to date should be regarded as preliminary and subject to review over time. The lower-than-expected CO2 emission level is caused by the available types of subprojects in water treatment and minihydro, which do not produce significant emission reduction. However, this number is yet to be adjusted at the end of the project closure. Data Source: SIO-GFF progress reporting included in PT SMI's annual reports Actual value:
